title: Progressive degradation layers and automatic shunt policy for hosted chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
PRD: Define explicit SLO bands, error-budget-driven degradation layers, and an automated traffic-shunt (fallback) orchestration policy for Hosted Chat endpoints. Goal: keep user-visible failures minimal while preserving overall platform availability and unit economics. This ticket captures the acceptance criteria, metrics, rollout gates, and operational hooks required to ship an automated degradation+traffic-shift capability that can be enabled per-tenant and globally for hosted chat routes.

Background: Hosted chat workloads are latency-sensitive but sometimes encounter capacity or model regressions that require graceful degradation (reduced feature set or lower-cost model variant) or automated shunting to fallback regions/capacity tiers. Current rollout practices are manual and slow; we need codified thresholds so runtime can make safe, observable decisions.

Scope:
- Define SLOs (latency percentiles, availability, error budgets) for interactive chat (short context <= 512 tokens) across three tiers (Gold, Standard, Bulk).
- Define three progressive degradation layers (Layer 0: full functionality, Layer 1: reduced beam/temperature/response-structure, Layer 2: fallback model or reduced context + token budget).
- Define automated shunt/orchestration policy that shifts traffic to fallback model/region/dedicated capacity when error budget burn or latency breach thresholds are met.
- Specify rollout gates for enabling this feature (canary schedule, monitoring, manual override, telemetry requirements).

Out of scope: per-tenant billing changes, on-prem private deployment specifics (handled in separate PM ticket), long-context (>2048 tokens) chat flows (handled later).

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Runtime Eng (Liam Chen), Observability (Nora Singh), Design (Marcus Velasquez), SRE (Priya Rao), Legal/Compliance (for data residency checks).

Artifacts: Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HI/Progressive+Degradation+PRD, Design frames: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/deg-playbook, Initial runtime ADR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/adr/pull/98, Observability dashboard draft: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/hosted-chat/degradation-playbook.

Acceptance summary: System automatically transitions between layers with defined safety checks, emits clear signals to Console and alerts, and can be toggled by tenant. Must pass load, regression, and chaos tests.
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions documented and stored in config-service: p50 <= 120ms (Gold),  p95 <= 400ms (Gold), p99 <= 900ms (Gold); Standard and Bulk bands documented similarly.
Availability SLO: 99.95% per-month for Gold, 99.9% Standard, 99.5% Bulk. Error budget windows and burn calculations available in Console.
Three degradation layers implemented with runtime toggles and per-tenant flags. Each layer has explicit behavioral spec and fallbacks listed in Confluence.

Automated shunt policy implemented: when 1-hour rolling burn rate >= 4x and p99 latency > threshold for 15m, begin staged shunt (10% -> 25% -> 100%) to fallback variant with exponential backoff if error budget continues to burn.
Canary rollout gates: initial canary at 5% traffic for 60 minutes with no >2x expected burn and p99 within 1.25x of baseline; automated rollback to full if threshold breached.

Observability: Console shows error budget curve, per-tenant latency histograms, degradation-layer counts, and a time-series for shunt events. Every shunt must create an incident stub with tags for affected tenants.
Contract tests: CI includes per-route contract tests for structured output and latency-instrumented smoke tests. PRs must include synthetic traffic run demonstrating expected degradation behavior.

Load and chaos testing: run k6 load job at 2x expected peak and inject latency/failure in the model-serving layer; system must transition to Layer 1 or fallback without user-facing 5xx rate increase >0.5% over baseline.
Manual override and tenant opt-out: Console toggle to opt tenant out of automated shunts; admin endpoint for immediate rollback documented with RBAC controls.
Documentation: customer-facing KB explaining what each degradation layer means for users and what to expect in Console; internal runbook for SRE with escalation flow.
rollout_gates: Telemetry completeness: p95/p99 latency and request success metrics must be present for target route for 7 days before feature enablement.
Canary phase 1: enable for internal tenants (10%) for 72h, require no >0.2% uptick in user-facing 5xx and no sustained error budget burn >1.5x baseline.
Canary phase 2: expand to self-serve tenants (30%) for 24h, require stability and manual signoff from PM and SRE.
Full rollout: ramp to 100% with progressive monitoring checkpoints (1h, 6h, 24h) and automated rollback if burn rate thresholds or p99 regressions occur.
Safety net: must be able to disable automated shunt globally within 5 minutes via operator runbook and admin API.
metrics_to_monitor: Error budget remaining (%) by tenant and aggregate
Request and token cost delta after degradation
implementation_notes: Runtime must support configuration-driven layer definitions (json config) and expose a deterministic decision path given metrics windows.
Prefer non-blocking transitions: use traffic percentage-based shunt with gradual increase and monitoring pauses between steps.
Fallback variants should default to quantized or lower-context models already verified for semantic parity tests.
Console needs a new visualization for 'Degradation heatmap' and event timeline; discuss with Design (DES-34012) for UX.
SRE to own runbook and PagerDuty play for any automated shunt that affects >5% of production traffic.
Add feature flagging in admin service to enable/disable per-tenant and globally; ensure audit logs are emitted for toggles.
